headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty plunged as Indian benchmarks posted their longest weekly losing run in 25 years

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Aggressive selling by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) and FPIs
Concerns over rising inflation and potential RBI rate hikes flagged by SBI Research
Global economic risks and surging fuel prices following G7 oil release news
Negative sentiment in international markets including cues from DJIA and NASDAQ
whatHappening: The Sensex and Nifty extended their losing streak to an eighth consecutive week
Approximately Rs 9 lakh crore in investor wealth was wiped out in a single session crash
FPIs turned net sellers in September, pulling out a total of ₹35,860 crore
Indian benchmark shares recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
summary: Indian markets are closed for Gandhi Jayanti following a session where the Sensex and Nifty hit a 25-year weekly losing streak. Heavy FII selling and inflation concerns wiped out Rs 9 lakh crore in investor wealth during the last trading day. Markets will remain shut until Tuesday, October 6.
